submission.natural_language_explanation: L13/H7 is a preceding-nominal copy head with a first-token sink: it writes near its mean while attending the text's first token, and at a token that follows a noun phrase - the finite verb of that phrase's clause, or a possessive 's, preposition, particle, determiner, conjunction or following word right after the phrase - it locks onto the phrase's head noun (its last token, 1-13 tokens back) and copies that noun's value into the residual (OV copying +0.31), crossing the active line only where 0.6-0.95 of its attention lands on one content noun. Such decisive locks are the rule for a possessive's noun (the economy's outlook, Lee's loss, the judge's final order), for a person, role or animal subject at its verb (the judge signed, the clerk filed, the nurse recorded, the postman slipped, the waiter handed) and for a dependent or predicate after a noun that sits four or more tokens into the text (the fog lifted off, the last light left the room, the case sat open, the box having, the college team), so an ordinary multi-clause prompt is usually active somewhere (the head is active at about 9% of scanned tokens), while the sink beats a weak mass or abstract noun that opens the text at its first verb (the weather improved, the music stopped, the gate swung open, the engine hummed), a retrieved quantifier or demonstrative pronoun (everyone, that) stays at the floor because its value is near the mean, and function-word-only text and existential 'there is/are' frames with inanimate nominals never supply a decisive lock.

rival_explanations: A recency-only copy head with no noun-phrase or subject structure: it copies whatever content token it read most recently (noun, verb or adverb) and its write only reflects that token's key match, so an inanimate mass subject at its first verb ('the weather improved', 'the music stopped') should fire as strongly as 'the judge signed'.

A lexical-distance head: the write strength is just how far the attended token's value sits from the head's mean output, so rarity or surprise in context decides activity rather than syntax, and a rare noun should fire wherever it is retrieved (even as the text's first subject) while a common one should stay at the floor even in a second clause.
